verdict: EchoStar's revenue fell 69% to $1.1B after it deconsolidated its pay-TV and most of its broadband businesses, yet it booked a $2.8B profit — almost entirely a $3.1B gain on selling wireless spectrum licenses to AT&T.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: $1,128M, -69% YoY — most of the drop is businesses deconsolidated in 2026, not lost sales

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.note: $2,782M — almost all of it one-off deal gains, not money from customers

kpis.label: AT&T spectrum gain
kpis.note: $3,107M gain on selling 3.45 GHz and 600 MHz spectrum licenses to AT&T (closed July 28, 2026)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Vs a loss of $44.37 a year ago, when the company booked a huge impairment

segments.name: AT&T spectrum gain
segments.note: EchoStar sold all its 3.45 GHz and 600 MHz spectrum licenses to AT&T (the deal closed July 28, 2026) for $20.25B in cash and booked a $3,107M gain — the sale value minus what the licenses were carried at on its books. Spectrum licenses are the airwaves mobile networks run on. This one gain is 276% of the quarter's revenue.

segments.name: Deconsolidation gain
segments.note: A $439M accounting gain from deconsolidating the pay-TV and broadband subsidiaries in 2026 ($10,168M over the first nine months). No cash arrived — EchoStar still owns and runs those businesses, but their results no longer count in its reported revenue or costs. The gain is 39% of revenue.

segments.name: Wireless
segments.note: Mobile phone service (including the Boost Mobile business) and devices sold to subscribers — now 80% of all revenue after the other businesses were deconsolidated.

segments.name: Broadband and Satellite Services
segments.note: Satellite broadband and communications services (the Hughes business). Most of this segment was deconsolidated on July 31, 2026, so only part of the quarter is included.

segments.name: Pay-TV
segments.note: The DISH and Sling TV businesses. Substantially all of this segment was deconsolidated on June 30, 2026, so Q3 holds only a small remainder.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Mostly leased spectrum revenue and equipment and other sales outside the three main segments — the jump reflects spectrum leasing after the deconsolidations.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company, including $130M of subscriber acquisition costs (the cost of signing up new wireless customers).

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of satellites, network gear and other long-lived assets over their lives — far lower than a year ago because the deconsolidated businesses took their assets with them.

opex.name: Impairments and other
opex.note: Write-downs of assets in the broadband business — tiny next to the $16.5B of impairments booked in the same quarter a year ago.

otherDetail: Other income was $3,251M, net: a $3,107M gain on the AT&T spectrum sale and a $439M deconsolidation gain, plus $106M of interest income, minus $312M of interest expense and $89M of other net costs. It also reflects a $0.1M loss attributable to noncontrolling interests, so the flow lands on the $2,782M profit attributable to EchoStar.
oneTimers: A $3,107M gain on the AT&T Transactions: EchoStar sold all its 3.45 GHz and 600 MHz spectrum licenses to AT&T, closing July 28, 2026, and received $20.25B in cash (a further $2.4B went into an FCC-mandated trust for wireless creditors). Spectrum licenses are the airwaves mobile networks run on — this sale is the quarter.

A $439M deconsolidation gain in Q3 ($10,168M over the first nine months). EchoStar still owns and manages the deconsolidated DISH/pay-TV and broadband subsidiaries, but their results no longer count in EchoStar's reported revenue or costs — which is why revenue fell 69% year over year.
footerNote: EchoStar filed no separate earnings release for Q3 2026; every figure is from its Form 10-Q filed November 3, 2026. Segment figures are revenues from external customers in the 10-Q segment note (intersegment revenue excluded). Amounts are in $M to three decimals, as reported in thousands in the 10-Q. Chart adaptation: because net other income ($3,251M) is nearly three times revenue, this page anchors its chart on total money in — revenue plus the $3,107M AT&T spectrum gain and the $439M deconsolidation gain ($4,674M in all). Chart percentages are shares of total money in; node notes also give true shares of revenue. The $295M of interest and other net costs and the quarter's tax are shown charged against the gains. Reported figures are unchanged: revenue $1,128M, gross profit $477M, operating income $148M, net income $2,782M. One-off gains are orange; real sales are blue.
follow100Note: Adapted for EchoStar: this table is per $100 of total money in (revenue + the two one-off gains), not per $100 of revenue — per $100 of revenue alone, the spectrum gain would be about $276 and the table would be meaningless. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: A much smaller company on paper
takeaways.text: Revenue fell from $3,614M to $1,128M. Pay-TV was deconsolidated on June 30, 2026 and most of Broadband and Satellite Services on July 31 — EchoStar still owns and runs those businesses, but accounting rules no longer fold their sales into its results. Wireless, down just 3% to $905M, is now the core.

takeaways.title: The spectrum sale is the profit
takeaways.text: Selling its 3.45 GHz and 600 MHz licenses to AT&T produced a $3,107M gain, and deconsolidation added a further $439M gain. Together they turned $148M of operating income into a $2,782M net profit — one-off deal gains, not money from customers.

takeaways.title: Cash in, debt story changed
takeaways.text: AT&T paid $20.25B in cash at closing, with another $2.4B placed in an FCC-mandated trust for wireless creditors. Interest expense still cost $312M in the quarter, but the spectrum proceeds transform a balance sheet that a year ago supported a $12.8B quarterly loss.

adaptation: Standard layout adapted: the chart anchors on total money in (revenue $1,127.6M + AT&T spectrum gain $3,107.0M + deconsolidation gain $439.0M = $4,673.6M) because EchoStar's net other income ($3,251.3M) is nearly three times its revenue. Flow balance checks on the adapted model: total money in = left after direct costs + cost of revenue ($4,673.6M = $4,022.8M + $650.8M); left after direct costs = one-off gains + operating income + operating expenses ($4,022.8M = $3,546.0M + $147.8M + $329.0M); operating income + other income - tax = net income ($147.8M + $3,251.3M - $616.8M = $2,782.2M), with the $294.7M of interest and other net costs and the $616.8M tax shown charged against the gains. Reported figures are unchanged: revenue $1,127.6M, gross profit $476.8M, operating income $147.8M, net income $2,782.2M.
